hierarchy.original_event: A rubber ball is dropped onto a hard floor, bouncing four times with decreasing height before coming to rest.

catalog.name: vertical_bounce
catalog.applicability: Passive vertical drop/rebound process on a fixed flat surface, with one or more contacts. Point-body approximation without spin. Not active dribbling or later rolling.

catalog.name: free_fall
catalog.applicability: Free vertical flight ending at first surface contact. No impact vibration is generated by this model; split off a subsequent impact when needed.

catalog.name: single_impact
catalog.applicability: One isolated normal impact against a fixed surface. Does not include repeated action or a separately described ringing tail.

catalog.name: sliding
catalog.applicability: Horizontal sliding/dragging with Coulomb friction, either unpowered coasting or externally maintained constant speed. Not rolling or arbitrary varying force.

catalog.name: rolling
catalog.applicability: Horizontal rolling with effective constant rolling-resistance deceleration. No bounce-to-roll conversion is inferred.

catalog.name: damped_oscillation
catalog.applicability: One decaying ringing/vibration tail after excitation. The excitation impact itself must be separate if also requested.

catalog.name: periodic
catalog.applicability: Continuous steady periodic vibration of a motor/tool. Uses a sinusoidal carrier. Not a small count of distinct knocks.

catalog.name: stochastic
catalog.applicability: Irregular independent contacts such as sparse raindrops/gravel, represented by a Poisson process or its fixed-count conditional form.

catalog.name: rhythmic_action
catalog.applicability: Intentional repeated knocks/steps/taps, including active dribbling. Cadence is behavioral, not passive restitution.

notes: Assumed constant restitution, a rigid stationary floor, no drag and instantaneous contact.
Material names describe the impact caption; they do not determine a calibrated restitution coefficient.
Pulse duration is a rendering choice, not predicted physical contact time.
Intensity is normalized impulse, not measured acceleration or perceived strength.
The requested/rendered contact count is not a prediction of when the ball stops.
The excerpt ends just after its last collision; this is not physical rest or a bounce-to-roll conversion.
Source/parameter extraction is an LM judgment. Defaults are unmeasured assumptions.
Normalized amplitude is not calibrated perceived strength or cross-model force.
